business_problem: ServiceNow wanted to solve complex operational problems across IT, employee, sales, and developer workflows, starting with a need to make its IT service desk more efficient and then reduce manual work, improve self-service, and help staff find and produce information faster.
solution_summary: ServiceNow describes a multi-use-case generative AI deployment running on the Now Platform across its own operations as a first-party adopter. The implementation builds on earlier machine learning in Predictive Intelligence, which predicts business service and routes incidents to the right assignment groups, and extends that foundation with AI Search, AI Search with GenAI, Now Assist for IT Service Management, Now Assist for Creator, and the Generative AI Controller. User questions, incident work notes, and knowledge content are processed inside Now Platform workflows; AI Search with GenAI sends retrieved information to an LLM to synthesize a single actionable answer with follow-up Q&A, while Now Assist summarizes incident histories for agents and converts natural-language prompts into code suggestions for developers. Generative AI Controller acts as the reusable integration layer for connecting ServiceNow instances to domain-specific or general-purpose LLMs so teams can embed generation into workflows such as knowledge base content creation without rebuilding integrations each time.

AI Search with GenAI retrieves supporting information and sends it to an LLM for synthesis into a single answer, while Now Assist summarizes work notes or converts developer prompts into code suggestions. The outputs are then returned to employees, agents, developers, and the sales team inside their existing ServiceNow workflows.
